title: Batch 9 Acts + Paul Historical-Geography Curation Methodology
notes: Separates canonical narrative geography, Pauline self-reference, independent ancient testimony, inscriptions, archaeology, later tradition, and route reconstruction. Exact roads, houses, prisons, wreck sites, and martyrdom locations remain unpinned unless evidence supports a location.
verificationNote: Project-authored curation methodology; no external source verification claim is implied.

title: Acts of the Apostles — canonical geographic sequence
notes: Project-authored summaries and references only. Acts provides the main narrative sequence for Batch 9; route lines are generalized visualizations, not recovered GPS tracks.

title: Pauline letters — canonical geographic and chronological references
notes: Used for Paul’s own geographic references and letter-recipient context. The atlas does not force disputed correlations between Acts and Galatians or assign exact composition sites where scholarship is divided.

title: Josephus, Jewish Antiquities, Book 19
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Ancient literary source for Agrippa I, Claudian-era Judea, and Agrippa’s death at Caesarea.

title: Josephus, Jewish Antiquities, Book 20
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Ancient literary source for the Claudian famine, high priest Ananias, Felix, Festus, and Agrippa II-era chronology.

title: Josephus, Jewish War, Book 2
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Ancient literary context for Roman Judea, procurators, Caesarea, and Agrippa II.

title: Delphi inscription / Claudius letter mentioning Gallio
notes: Key external chronological anchor for Gallio’s proconsulship of Achaia, commonly used to constrain Paul’s Corinthian chronology. The inscription does not mention Paul.

title: Suetonius, Claudius 25.4
author: Suetonius
notes: Reports Claudius expelling Jews from Rome because of disturbances associated with “Chrestus.” The relationship to Acts 18 and exact date are interpreted cautiously.

title: 1 Clement 5
notes: Early Christian memory of Peter and Paul’s suffering. Used only for later reception context; Acts itself ends with Paul alive under house arrest in Rome.

title: Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World — eastern Mediterranean and Roman road geography
notes: Reference framework for established Greco-Roman cities, regions, and transport geography. No proprietary map imagery is bundled.

title: The Book of Acts in the Setting of Hellenistic History
author: Colin J. Hemer
notes: Historical-geographic synthesis used cautiously for Acts place names, travel sequences, titles, and chronology.

title: Anatolia: Land, Men, and Gods in Asia Minor
author: Stephen Mitchell
notes: Regional historical framework for Roman Asia Minor, Galatia, Pisidia, Lycaonia, roads, and civic geography.

title: Roman roads and itineraries of Asia Minor — scholarly synthesis
notes: Used only for generalized corridor reconstruction. The atlas does not claim Paul followed a specific surviving paved alignment unless Acts states a route.

title: Roman Cyprus archaeological and historical synthesis
notes: Supports Salamis, Paphos, and provincial context. It does not identify every Acts episode with a specific building.

title: Pisidian Antioch archaeological and epigraphic research
notes: Supports the established city site and Roman colonial setting; the precise synagogue of Acts 13 is not identified.

title: Lystra and Derbe historical-geographic research
notes: Lystra is commonly associated with the Hatunsaray/Zoldera mound area; Derbe remains debated, with Kerti Höyük among major proposals. Candidate geometry is labeled accordingly.

title: Philippi archaeological and Roman-colony research
notes: Supports the established city and colonial landscape; the exact riverside prayer place and prison of Acts are not recoverable.

title: Via Egnatia historical-road research
notes: Supports the broad east-west corridor through Macedonia. Journey polylines remain schematic rather than surveyed reconstructions of Paul’s footsteps.

title: Roman-period Athens and Areopagus topographic research
notes: Supports the physical Hill of Ares and civic context. Acts’ phrase “Areopagus” can denote the council/body as well as the hill, so the speech is not pinned to one exact spot.

title: Roman Corinth archaeological and epigraphic research
notes: Supports Corinth, Cenchreae, the forum/bema, and Gallio-era civic setting. The bema is a plausible forum setting, not archaeologically proven as Paul’s exact hearing position.

title: Ephesus archaeological and epigraphic research
notes: Supports the city, theater, Artemision, and Roman provincial setting. The hall of Tyrannus and exact locations of individual house meetings remain unlocated.

title: Alexandria Troas archaeological and historical research
notes: Supports the major Roman city/port used in Acts. The exact upper room of Acts 20 is not located.

title: Caesarea Maritima Roman-period archaeology
notes: Supports the harbor city, administrative role, and first-century built environment. Individual prison rooms or audience halls used for Paul are not identified as certain.

title: Roman Damascus urban-topography research
notes: Supports Damascus and the east-west Roman street axis underlying later Straight Street. Acts’ house of Judas and exact conversion location are not recoverable.

title: Acts 27 ancient-navigation and Malta shipwreck scholarship
notes: Used to model the voyage as a schematic maritime route. Malta is the mainstream identification of Melite; the exact wreck bay and anchors are not archaeologically demonstrated by Acts.

title: Ancient Mediterranean sailing and Roman maritime transport — historical synthesis
notes: Supports seasonal sailing constraints and broad corridors only; winds and currents make any single drawn track illustrative.

title: First-century Rome archaeological and historical topography
notes: Supports Rome, Via Appia approaches, and urban context. Acts gives no recoverable address for Paul’s rented lodging.

title: Lycus Valley cities — Colossae, Laodicea, Hierapolis historical geography
notes: Supports recipient geography for Pauline/Deutero-Pauline letters without claiming Acts narrates a visit to Colossae.

title: Claudian famine in Judea — Josephus and Roman-era chronological synthesis
notes: Relates Josephus’s famine notices to the broad Claudian period. It does not prove that every famine reference in Acts has one recoverable calendar year.

title: Pauline chronology — modern critical synthesis
notes: Uses Gallio as the strongest external anchor while treating most conversion, council, journey, arrest, Festus-accession, and voyage dates as conventional ranges rather than exact years.
